notes: L1 and L2 oracle: scip-dart 1.7.0 (tier A, Dart SDK 3.13.4, calibration/oracles/scip-dart), one index per package of eight pure-Dart packages (felangel/bloc bloc-v9.2.1 packages bloc, bloc_test, bloc_concurrency; dart-lang/http http-v1.5.0 pkgs http, http_parser, http2, web_socket_channel, http_multi_server), scored with -scip-defs, measured as cloned after `dart pub get` inside each package. universal-ctags 6.2.1 has no Dart parser, so no tier-B oracle exists; the packages that need the Flutter SDK (flutter_bloc, angular_bloc, cupertino_http, cronet_http, ok_http) are not measured, nor are hydrated_bloc and replay_bloc, whose workspace example depends on it.

L1: 2,064 SCIP definitions and 2,065 fathom definitions in the kind intersection, all 2,064 matched (sym_recall 1, sym_precision .9995, kind_agreement 1, range_agreement 1 on all 2,064, every one of 1,732 callables signed). The one dialect-only definition is http's library-private extension type `_IterableHeaders` (scip-dart writes a private definition as a local symbol of unspecified kind, which is not read as a definition). web_socket_channel's `signKey`, a comment between the signature and its `=>` body, is extracted since LB-F247 (one- and two-comment variants of the function and method patterns). scip:namespace (29) is a file or an `import ... as p` prefix and has no fathom symbol. A private member is a `local N` symbol in scip-dart; its kind says what it is, so a private field, accessor, method or variable is read as a definition (SCIPDefs) and a call inside a private method belongs to it (SCIPOptions.PrivateMembers).

L2: 3,133 call pairs in the truth, 3,124 found (call_recall .9971), 3,238 fathom pairs, 3,124 in the truth (call_precision .9648). 295 callable references are left out of the truth because no call is written at their range (a tear-off such as `onError: c.addError`, an operator, the super(...) of an initializer). The dialect's pairs outside the index are calls through a function-typed parameter or field (`emit(state)`, `handler(e)`, `onError(...)`), which are call sites in the source and references to a parameter in the index.

L3 (wave lx item dart, fathom cd4c1e9e): file_edge_recall .7844 (484 of 617 SCIP file edges) and file_edge_precision .9918 (484 of 488), from .3534 (422 of 1,194) and .9953. Two changes, both measured one at a time on the eight packages: (1) the oracle truth (LB-F245): scip-dart numbers `local N` symbols per document from 0, SCIP scopes a local symbol to its own document, and the file-edge truth looked every reference's symbol up in one map across documents, so a document's `local 3` was an edge to the first document that defined a private member as `local 3`: 577 of the 1,194 truth edges were such collisions (recall .3534 to .684 with truth 617, no extractor change); (2) the dialect (LB-F246): a library's `part 'x.dart';` re-exports the part's names and is a wildcard import of the part in the library, a part's `part of 'lib.dart';` is a wildcard import of its library (file_edge_recall .684 to .7844; 94 of the 195 missing pairs targeted a part file). The oracle cannot attest a private cross-file reference inside one library (its local symbols are document-scoped), so the 4 fathom-only file edges, all through a private top-level function a part calls (`_isFlagSet`, `TerminatedException`) or a `get(...)` call, count against precision though they are written in the source.

L3 classes left (133 truth pairs fathom draws no edge for; the written L3 ceiling, none needed for the grade): method, getter and field access on a typed receiver (`emit.isDone`, `response.statusCode`, `super.onChange(...)`, 17 + 11 + 12 pairs only these, about 33 + 23 + 18 with others), which needs a receiver's type; a doc-comment reference `[Request]` (scip-dart attests it, 26 pairs only these), which no tree-sitter query can capture as a name inside a comment node (an engine capture, O533); a part file reading a name its library imports (a part has no imports of its own, ~10 pairs: `Header` in frame_types.dart through frames.dart's `../hpack/hpack.dart`), which is the resolver's (O534); a lower case name an import brings in (`boundaryCharacters`, `isProtocolException`, an inherited getter `state`, ~25 pairs), dropped by the extractor's upper case rule where a wildcard import is the only binding (O535); a `show` name in an export statement (8 pairs, the export draws no file edge of its own, O535); a reference outside any definition (a top-level `@GenerateMocks([...])` annotation's arguments, 2 pairs, O536). Constructors, named constructors, enum values, extension members, `@Foo` annotations and prefixed names leave no residual of their own: every miss in those classes is one of the above.

L4 (S1, LB-F239, cherry-picked from wave lx item python): typed_recall .9762 (10,346 of 10,598 in-index edges), from .8464; 4,266 references to a parameter or a type parameter are out of the denominator (scip_edges_param_target) and def_mapping reads 1 (2,064 of 2,064). The 252 edges left unmapped are 242 references to an `import ... as p` prefix (a Namespace symbol: scip-dart defines it, fathom has no symbol for a prefix, `http.get(...)` in a test) and 10 inside a definition that is not mapped (a local closure, O537).

import_resolution reads 1 on 6 of 772 imports (.8%): scip-dart attests an import only where a `show` or `hide` name is a reference (O244), so 409 in-repo imports resolve to a file of the subject with no attestation and import edges read precision .0145 (6 of 415). The reading is thin, not wrong; no guard is built (the oracle's reach, not the dialect's, bounds it).
